content: Your doctor has prescribed torsemide to help reduce the amount of excess fluid in your body. This medication can be administered in one of two ways: it may be added to an intravenous (IV) fluid that is delivered through a needle or catheter placed in your vein, or it may be injected directly into your vein or catheter over a period of at least two minutes. In some cases, torsemide may be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about this, consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Your healthcare provider, which may include your doctor, nurse, or pharmacist, will monitor the effectiveness of your treatment and check for any side effects. This will involve laboratory tests and physical examinations. It is crucial to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and the laboratory. The duration of your treatment will depend on how your body responds to the medication. Precautions Before Taking Torsemide: Inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to torsemide, any sulfa drugs, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially dexamethasone (Decadron), digoxin (Lanoxin), medications for high blood pressure, indomethacin (Indocin), lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid), prednisone, probenecid (Benemid), and any vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of diabetes, gout, or kidney or liver problems. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. If you become pregnant while on torsemide, contact your doctor immediately. Administering Torsemide: Before using torsemide, carefully inspect the solution. It should be clear and free of any floating particles. Gently squeeze the IV bag or examine the solution container to ensure there are no leaks. Do not use the solution if it is discolored, contains particles, or if the bag or container is leaking. Instead, use a new solution and show the damaged one to your healthcare provider. It is essential to follow your healthcare provider’s instructions precisely when using this medication. Do not alter your dosing schedule without consulting your provider. If you experience a mechanical issue, such as a blockage in the tubing, needle, or catheter, your healthcare provider may instruct you to stop the infusion. If this happens, contact your provider immediately to ensure your therapy can continue without interruption. Side Effects: Minor Side Effects: Torsemide may cause some side effects. Notify your healthcare provider if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: Frequent urination Muscle cramps Weakness Dizziness Faintness Fatigue Headache Confusion Thirst Upset stomach Vomiting Severe Side Effects: If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your healthcare provider immediately: Rapid or excessive weight loss Vomiting blood If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Storing Your Medication: Your healthcare provider may supply you with several days’ worth of torsemide at a time. Store the medication exactly as directed. Ensure you understand the proper storage requirements for the medication. Keep your supplies in a clean, dry place when not in use, and always store medications and supplies out of the reach of children. Your healthcare provider will instruct you on how to safely dispose of used needles, syringes, tubing, and containers to prevent accidental injury. In Case of Emergency or Overdose: If you suspect an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 or your local emergency services immediately. Signs of Infection: If you are receiving torsemide through a vein or under your skin, it is important to recognize the symptoms of a catheter-related infection. This type of infection occurs at the site where the needle enters your vein or skin.
